# linux_partition (Resource)

Makes sure a partition exists on a disk, with `sfdisk`. Only GPT partition tables are supported.

Existing data is never overwritten: a partition that already exists is kept as it is, apart from its type, its name and growing it; a disk without partition table only gets one when it holds nothing, as `blkid` sees it. A disk that holds a file system directly is refused. Partitions are never shrunk, moved or deleted: destroying the resource leaves the partition on the disk.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One partition using the whole disk. If the disk already has a partition 1,
# it is kept as it is: its data is never touched.
resource "linux_partition" "data" {
  device = "/dev/disk/by-id/nvme-Amazon_Elastic_Block_Store_vol0abc123"
  number = 1
  name   = "data"
}

# A 4 GiB swap partition followed by a partition filling the rest of the
# disk, which grows when the disk is enlarged.
resource "linux_partition" "swap" {
  device = "/dev/sdc"
  number = 1
  size   = "4G"
  type   = "swap"
}

resource "linux_partition" "rest" {
  device = "/dev/sdc"
  number = 2

  depends_on = [linux_partition.swap]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device` (String) Disk to partition, such as `/dev/sdb` or a stable path under `/dev/disk/by-id/`. The resource waits up to 2 minutes for it to appear, for volumes being attached.
- `number` (Number) Partition number, from 1.

### Optional

- `name` (String) GPT partition name, available as `/dev/disk/by-partlabel/<name>`.
- `size` (String) Size, such as `512M`, `20G` or `1T` (powers of 1024). Defaults to all the free space after the start of the partition: the partition then grows when the disk is enlarged and the space after it is free. A larger size grows the partition; a smaller one is an error.
- `type` (String) Partition type: `bios_boot`, `efi`, `linux`, `lvm`, `raid`, `swap`, or a GPT type GUID. Defaults to `linux`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Disk and partition number, such as `/dev/sdb:1`.
- `path` (String) Device path of the partition, such as `/dev/sdb1` or `/dev/nvme1n1p1`.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Size of the partition, in bytes. Reference it in the `triggers` of `linux_filesystem` to grow the file system with the partition.
- `uuid` (String) Unique partition GUID (`PARTUUID`).
